issues.legal_issue: Convictions for theft and unlawful assembly to commit theft cannot stand when possession of the land and crop was seriously disputed and the accused may have acted under a bona fide belief that they were entitled to possession.
material_facts: The complainant claimed that he had received possession of the land through execution proceedings and had cultivated the crop that the accused harvested.
The other widow of the former tenant had consistently disputed the complainant’s right to the land and claimed to have remained in possession through cultivators.

The land was submerged for several years and later re-emerged; revenue and magistrate proceedings, along with rent receipts, supported the other widow’s claim to actual possession after it re-emerged.
The evidence did not establish beyond controversy that the complainant possessed the land or cultivated the crop when it was harvested.
The accused claimed to be cultivating the land for the other widow, and the Court considered it impossible to rule out their bona fide belief that they were entitled to possession.
issues.conclusion: The convictions and sentences could not be upheld and were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 379 and 143 of the Penal Code, the convictions could not be sustained on a partial view of the evidence where the complainant’s possession and ownership of the crop were seriously doubtful and the accused may have believed in good faith that they were entitled to possession. The Court relied on the evidence of the competing possession claims and the related proceedings; it cited no earlier cases for this principle.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_theft_and_unlawful_: The proceeding is a criminal appeal challenging convictions for theft and unlawful assembly to commit theft.
predicates.possession_was_seriously_disputed: The accused or a person through whom they claimed cultivation disputed the complainant’s possession of the land.
predicates.complainant_possession_was_not_establish: The evidence left the complainant’s actual possession of the land and cultivation of the crop uncertain.
predicates.accused_may_have_believed_they_were_enti: The accused claimed to cultivate the land for a person asserting possession, and the evidence did not rule out their bona fide belief that they were entitled to possess it.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal challenges theft and unlawful assembly convictions, and possession is seriously disputed, the complainant’s possession is unproven beyond controversy, and the accused may have believed they were entitled to possession, the convictions are set aside.

issues.legal_issue: Concurrent factual findings may be reopened in a special-leave appeal when material evidence was not properly considered and that omission may have caused the parties’ positions to be misjudged.
material_facts: The Trial Magistrate and the appellate court made concurrent findings that the complainant possessed the land and that the accused took his crop.
The High Court dismissed the revision on the ground that it could not interfere with those concurrent findings.
The Supreme Court examined court proceedings and other documentary evidence that had not received proper attention and that cast substantial doubt on the findings about possession.
issues.conclusion: Although ordinarily reluctant to reopen concurrent findings of fact under Article 136, the Court reopened them in this case because material evidence had not been properly considered.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 136 of the Constitution, the Court is ordinarily reluctant to reopen concurrent findings of fact, but may do so where material evidence was not given proper attention, resulting in a misjudgment of the parties’ positions. No earlier cases were cited for this principle.

predicates.special_leave_appeal_from_criminal_convi: The proceeding is a special-leave appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.lower_courts_made_concurrent_factual_fin: The trial court and the appellate court reached the same factual findings.
predicates.material_evidence_was_not_properly_consi: Relevant evidence bearing on the parties’ positions did not receive proper attention in the lower courts.

issues.definition: In a special-leave appeal from a criminal conviction, concurrent factual findings may be reopened when material evidence was not properly considered.
